text:
Maya Chen: Heads up — new int8 canary (canary-aurora-int8) is showing a weird pattern: successful JSON toolcall in logs then client retries and we see duplicate tool invocations.
Tony Alvarez: Hmm, saw a spike in downstream charges?
Maya Chen: Yes, per-route cost doubled for a subset of requests hitting the canary. Latency + retries look correlated.
Sophia Li: Do we have an example request/response?
Maya Chen: Pasted one from the canary traces:
```
REQUEST id=abc123 prompt=... tool=charge-card
MODEL RESPONSE (streamed):
{"action":"charge","amount":49.99,"card_id":"card_zzz"}\n<stream cut>
CLIENT logged parse error -> sent retry
SECOND MODEL RESPONSE (complete):
{"action":"charge","amount":49.99,"card_id":"card_zzz","tx_id":"tx_987"}
```
Tony Alvarez: So the prefix contained valid JSON but streaming cut caused client to treat it as truncated/invalid, so retry sent. Meanwhile the first partial JSON was actually valid and the tool already executed.
Ryan Patel: That matches our tracing: function invoke recorded at 1719765435 and again at 1719765440 for same request id.
Sophia Li: Why did the client decide it was an error if the prefix was valid JSON? Any stray control chars or multi-line tokens?
Maya Chen: The SDK has a naive check: it waits for closing brace in stream, but when stream cut happened mid-footer, our prefix had a closing brace because the model duplicated a small payload, but the stream ended with no newline and the SDK checks final checksum header which was missing -> treat as parse failure.
Tony Alvarez: So we get false-negative parse failure. Client retries, model returns full JSON, tool double-invoked.
Ryan Patel: Is this specific to int8 canary? We should compare with float baseline.
Maya Chen: Yes — baseline float model shows far fewer partial-stream anomalies. Canary int8 has higher probability of early EOS/internal buffer cut. Might be quantization kernel producing small truncation bursts.
Sophia Li: Proposed mitigations: 1) server-side de-dup for idempotent tool invocations using request-id + model-seq; 2) client-side smarter stream validation: accept valid JSON if parseable, but verify finalization via a lightweight checksum if present; 3) runtime retry suppression for known side-effecting tools. Thoughts?
Tony Alvarez: All 3 seem reasonable. We should prioritize server-side idempotency for side-effectful tools (payments). Can we get a cheap signature to detect duplicates?
Ryan Patel: We already log model-generated tx_id in successful toolcall payloads. Server can check if tx_id already recorded and skip second. But in the prefix case tx_id absent, so we need request-id idempotency too.
Maya Chen: I sketched a quick patch for runtime: if a tool invocation occurs and there is a prior invocation for same request-id within 10s, mark duplicate and don't forward to upstream. Pseudo: 
```
if seen_tool_call(request_id, tool_name):
    respond_with_cached_result()
else:
    forward()
    record_tool_call(request_id, tool_name)
```
Sophia Li: That helps hosted API but not Private deployments unless they opt-in. Also watch out for memory blowup storing request ids. Use TTL+LRU.
Tony Alvarez: Agree. Also we should tune client SDK: if stream ends but we received valid JSON and the trailing checksum is missing, maybe try single automatic parse-repair instead of full retry. e.g., attempt JSON.parse on accumulated bytes and accept if valid, else retry.
Maya Chen: Another angle: model-side fix. Investigate quant kernel that ends streams prematurely. I opened a profiler job on the canary pod: https://ci.redwood/ci/aurora-int8/1234 (deploy-bot posted).
deploy-bot: Canary rollout paused at 10% after metric threshold breach (parse-retry-rate > 0.8%). See rollout dashboard.
Ryan Patel: Good call to pause. Need triage owner for root cause analysis.
Maya Chen: I'll take lead on model + runtime triage. Ryan can help with tracing/telemetry. Sophia if you can prototype SDK guard. Tony can own server idempotency design.
Sophia Li: I can PR a quick client-side heuristic today. Keep it opt-in behind config flag.
Tony Alvarez: I'll draft runtime patch with TTL store and safe default 5s window.
Ryan Patel: I'll compile a sample set of affected request_ids and correlate with quantization config (per-layer int8 scale tables).
Maya Chen: Action items: Maya - model kernel traces + repro; Ryan - request id set + traces; Tony - runtime idempotency design PR; Sophia - SDK heuristic PR.
Maya Chen: Also we should update evals: add a structured-output-canary test that simulates stream cuts and checks for duplicate side-effects.
Sophia Li: I'll add a JSTest harness case for that.
Maya Chen: Thanks all. If we need to roll back canary, ops-bot pls standby.
ops-bot: Noted — rollback checklist reachable at https://internal/ops/rollbacks. Use /ops rollback canary-aurora-int8 if needed. :ok_hand: 
Tony Alvarez: Filing a follow-up ticket for long-term: kernel patch + formal idempotency contract for function/tool calls.
Maya Chen: Ticket created: https://tickets.redwood/ML-7842 (includes sample trace bundle).
Ryan Patel: Cool. Will reconvene tomorrow after initial PRs.
Maya Chen: End of thread — keeping channel updated. :slightly_smiling_face:
